content: Take this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not take a lower dose or stop taking this medication (or any other HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval, even for a short period. Do not increase your dose or take this medication more frequently than prescribed. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Headaches or difficulty sleeping may occur as side effects. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune system may cause symptoms. These reactions can occur at any time, whether shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication. For example, you may notice increased fat in the upper back and abdominal areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. Rilpivirine may commonly cause a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking rilpivirine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of rilpivirine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include dexamethasone, macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin), and rifamycins (such as rifampin and rifapentine). If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as viral load, T-cell counts, and liver function) should be conducted while you are taking this medication. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it with a meal as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours since the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication in its original bottle at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
